newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim says labour, spy laws can be debated.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim says labour, spy laws can be debated.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Tuesday offered to reopen parliamentary debate on a new labour law and another controversial bill boosting the powers of a domestic spy agency, a presidential spokesman said.

"Anything can be discussed in parliament again, whether it is the labour law or the law on the Agency for National Security Planning," the spokesman quoted Kim as telling opposition leaders in a meeting.
Both laws were rammed through parliament in a dawn session on December 26 while opposition deputies slept.
Kim said the labour legislation was aimed at revitalising the country's economy, but instead it had created problems for business by triggering wildcat strikes.
The spokesman said Kim rejected opposition demands that both laws be made void, saying this would be "unconstitutional".

Kim made the comments at a meeting with opposition leaders Kim Dae-jung of the National Congress for New Politics and Kim Jong-pil of the United Liberal Democratic Party. Lee Hong-koo, chairman of the ruling New Korea Party, also attended.
